title: Writing a marked word on a tape
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number, let $\Gamma$ be an alphabet, and let $x$ be an input word. Choose distinct work tapes $\mathrm{src},\mathrm{dst}$, symbols $\mathrm{zero},\mathrm{one}\in\Gamma$, and a nonempty word $w\in\Gamma^*$. Suppose a configuration $d$ starts in the copy phase, tape $\mathrm{src}$ agrees with the buffered word $w$ at every offset from $-1$ through $|w|$, and tape $\mathrm{dst}$ is blank at those offsets. After $4|w|+10$ steps, the machine is in its final phase and tape $\mathrm{dst}$ contains $\mathrm{one}$ followed by $|w|-1$ copies of $\mathrm{zero}$ on the $|w|$ cells beginning at its original head position; all other cells and configuration data are unchanged. This phase is not reached earlier, and every work-tape head stays within distance $|w|+1$ of its initial position at all times up to and including that time.
hypotheses_covered: distinct source and destination tape indices
initial state is the copy machine's sweep phase
source tape agrees with the buffered word at offsets $-1$ through $|w|$
destination tape is blank at offsets $-1$ through $|w|$
